subject: Throughput & headroom appraisal for Edison Labs commitment
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Karen Li <karen.li@edisonlabs.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edison capacity — quick ask on peak profile and SLOs

Karen — thanks for the call earlier. To make the Dedicated sizing proposal concrete for the Edison commitment, can you confirm two things so we can finalize GPU slab sizing and the canary plan:

1) Peak observed token-rate you expect during launch-week (tokens/sec). If you have a traffic schedule that shows a 24hr peak window, paste that number.
2) Target latency SLO (p95) for inference for the highest-importance route — we heard ~400ms but want final confirmation and whether you can tolerate occasional 2x degradation during incidents.

We want to validate a model-mix assumption before we run the slab calc (7b/13b/70b split). I'm attaching a draft calc — if you can return the peak token/sec and the SLO, we'll produce a recommended slab with headroom and a short canary runbook.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: edison_capacity_calc.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Karen Li <karen.li@edisonlabs.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@edisonlabs.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2028 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edison capacity — quick ask on peak profile and SLOs

Rishi — thanks. Quick replies below:

1) Peak: we project a launch-week crest of ~60,000 tokens/sec across all routes (this is a user-facing product spike; baseline expected to be ~15k t/s). The 60k number is conservative (includes a marketing-driven spike).
2) SLO: p95 <= 350ms on the primary /generate route; non-critical routes can accept up to 750ms p95. We can accept a short-lived 2x latency spike during incidents but would like automated fallbacks.

Also: model mix we plan to use initially — 55% redwood-7b-quant, 30% redwood-13b-quant, 15% redwood-70b-quant. Let me know if that changes sizing materially.

Karen
Karen Li
Head of Ops, Edison Labs

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Edison — initial slab math (draft)

Team — per Karen's inputs (peak 60k t/s, p95 350ms, model mix 55/30/15), I ran a quick capacity model. Key assumptions are in the attached spreadsheet and summarized below. This is a draft to align on the slab recommendation and the canary sizing before I send to the customer.

Assumptions used (conservative):
- Average tokens/request at peak: 140 tokens (customer-provided sample).
- Model effective throughput (tokens/sec per GPU, median observed on our preset kernels and 80GB A100 equivalent):
  * redwood-7b-quant: 20,000 t/s per GPU
  * redwood-13b-quant: 11,000 t/s per GPU
  * redwood-70b-quant: 1,800 t/s per GPU
- We assume horizontal scaling by model variant (no dynamic model sharding).
- Target headroom multiplier for safety and burst absorption: 1.3x (30%).

Calculation (weighted by model share of token traffic):
- Total peak tokens/sec: 60,000 t/s
- 7b share (55%): 33,000 t/s -> 33,000 / 20,000 = 1.65 -> round up to 2 GPUs
- 13b share (30%): 18,000 t/s -> 18,000 / 11,000 = 1.64 -> round up to 2 GPUs
- 70b share (15%): 9,000 t/s -> 9,000 / 1,800 = 5.0 -> round up to 5 GPUs
- Sum baseline GPUs = 9 GPUs
- Add 30% headroom -> 9 * 1.3 = 11.7 -> round up to 12 GPUs

Recommendation: provision a Dedicated slab of 12 x A100-80GB equivalent GPUs (logical GPU count).
Operational notes and tradeoffs:
- The 70b model is the dominant driver — if Edison can defer 70b traffic to a hosted fallback or quantized 13b variant during peak, we can reduce slab to ~7–8 GPUs (major cost savings).
- Canary: run a 4-GPU canary (1x 70b, 1x 13b, 2x 7b) for two full peak windows to validate p95 and cold-start behavior.
- Autoscale policy: allow burst-to-hosted-fallback at 1.5x peak for unexpected spikes; configure prefix caching on the 7b route to shave token throughput by ~12–18% based on their sample set.

I've attached the calc (edison_capacity_calc.xlsx) and a short canary runbook draft. If this looks reasonable I'll send the slab proposal to Karen with the cost delta and recommended commit tier.

— Rishi

Attachments: edison_capacity_calc.xlsx, canary-runbook.md
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Karen Li <karen.li@edisonlabs.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2028 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edison — initial slab math (draft)

Thanks Rishi — nice crisp calc. A few commercial notes:

1) Pricing: for a 12-GPU Dedicated slab we would propose two options (monthly reserve):
   a) 12x reserved (best-rate) — recommended for 12+ month commitment.
   b) 12x slab with burst pool (12 reserved + 4 shared burst GPUs) — provides cushion during short-term marketing spikes at a modest premium.
2) Canary credits: offer Edison two weeks of canary usage at 50% list price to smooth onboarding friction.
3) SLA: we should include an automated fallback policy in the contract (hosted fallback for 70b when dedicated is saturated). That satisfies their 2x spike tolerance while protecting latency SLO.

Priyom / Lauren — please add a short config snippet for the fallback route and the autoscale thresholds to the canary-runbook (Ben: I copied Karen on this mail so she can see the commercial options).

Ben Carter
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Karen Li <karen.li@edisonlabs.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edison — initial slab math (draft)

Appreciate the thoroughness. Edison is comfortable proceeding with the 12-GPU slab + burst option (12 reserved + 4 burst). We accept the canary credit offer. Next steps from our side: final PO by Friday and we want the canary window to start the following Tuesday (we'll provide test tokens and a 24hr peak schedule).

Two quick clarifications before I close the loop:
- Can you confirm how the 70b fallback to hosted will be routed (policy-based by latency or by util threshold)?
- For the canary, can Redwood run a live tracing hook to capture p95 across token buckets so our SRE can compare the two environments?

If you can answer those, we'll prep the PO.

Karen
Karen Li
Head of Ops, Edison Labs
